summary.short: Amends Sections 53B-26-301 and 53B-26-302 to establish a deep technology talent initiative, under which the board may fund employer-partnered deep technology programs at named Utah institutions of higher education, subject to appropriations and advisory council review. Effective 05/01/24.
summary.long: The instrument amends the definitions in Section 53B-26-301 and the deep technology initiative in Section 53B-26-302. Deep technology means technology leading to new products and innovations based on scientific discovery or meaningful engineering innovation; artificial intelligence is one of several listed fields it may include. Subject to appropriations, the board develops and oversees a talent initiative that funds expanded undergraduate and graduate programs and stackable credentials. An institution of higher education partnering with employers submits a proposal listing specified elements, such as enrollment estimates, employer commitments and requested funding. The advisory council reviews proposals against listed criteria and recommends funding; the board may fund programs on or before September 1 of each fiscal year. Funded institutions report annually to the board, which reports by November 1 each year to two legislative committees. The provisions set no sanctions. The advisory council is created in Section 53B-26-303, which is not in the text provided.
